# Proposed architecture decision

**Status: Proposed — project acceptance required.**

Engine 0.8.0; catalog 0.5.0; services 0.8.0; analysis 0.2.0.
Input SHA-256: 141cbf7df62d509c427c78109f5c030eeb1b61162dfa387db2ee5fe3002fbf28.

## Original result

PROVISIONAL STACK — unresolved critical constraints require review before production\. modular\_monolith recommendation selected from 18 complete compatible plans; month\-12 infrastructure planning band USD 1028\.89–3882\.82/month\.
Result: ok_with_warnings.

- frontend: Next\.js \+ React Native — Covers requested targets android, ios, web with ssr rendering\. Team languages: java, kotlin, typescript\. Selected after supporting\-service compatibility and whole\-plan infrastructure cost scoring\. Explicit critical warnings identify provisional data\-flow/control exceptions\.
- backend: Spring Boot — Provides a jvm application runtime for the fintech profile\. Language familiarity and delivery complexity were compared across compatible whole plans\. Selected after supporting\-service compatibility and whole\-plan infrastructure cost scoring\. Explicit critical warnings identify provisional data\-flow/control exceptions\.
- database: PostgreSQL — relational persistence via Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL\. The described ledger requires a reviewed relational profile\. Database drivers and host deployment were checked as a combination\. Selected after supporting\-service compatibility and whole\-plan infrastructure cost scoring\. Explicit critical warnings identify provisional data\-flow/control exceptions\.
- hosting: Amazon ECS / Fargate — Matches managed\_cloud with provider aws; reviewed primary compute region ap\-south\-1\. Required runtimes and separate database deployment were checked\. Selected after supporting\-service compatibility and whole\-plan infrastructure cost scoring\. Explicit critical warnings identify provisional data\-flow/control exceptions\.

Monthly infrastructure/operations band (activity fees additional): USD 1028.89–3882.82.

## Complete alternatives

- modular\_monolith\|next\-native\|spring\|pg\|ecs\|ap\-south\-1; score 85; USD 1028.89–3882.82; selected.
- modular\_monolith\|flutter\|spring\|pg\|ecs\|ap\-south\-1; score 78; USD 992.85–3810.74; alternative.
- modular\_monolith\|next\-native\|express\|pg\|ecs\|ap\-south\-1; score 78; USD 1028.89–3882.82; alternative.

## Preference stability

Original winner retained in 25/25 tested settings; 1 observed winners. Counts are not confidence probabilities.

## Cost assumptions

- Horizon: expected month\-12 footprint; 730 hours/month\. No tax, development/on\-call labor, domain registration or new on\-prem hardware procurement is included\.
- Peak concurrency supplied: 10000; not equated directly with requests/second\.
- RPS absent: authored daily\-active fraction 0\.2 of registered month\-12 users, floored at supplied peak concurrency \(60000 active/day\); 50 requests/active user/day gives 34\.722 average RPS\. Neither fraction nor request rate is measured; explicit RPS overrides both\. Peak capacity is separate\.
- Data volume 500 GB supplied; egress 3000 GB/month assumed at 0\.01 GB per year\-12 user, minimum 1 GB; backup retention 1 months assumed\.
- Compute provisioning hypothesis: 50 RPS or 1000 active users per reference allocation; WebSocket capacity is included in the peak\-concurrency replica floor, not charged again as per\-connection sidecars\. 13\.5 vCPU/2\-GiB\-equivalent units include frontend/backend, auth, workers, inference and telemetry once\. These are sizing assumptions requiring load tests, not capacity guarantees\.
- Billed duty 1–1; run polling workers with allocated CPU/minimum instances\. Higher availability adds at least two application allocations and in\-region database copies, but does not guarantee an SLA\. Rate bands include headroom; do not interpret reference regions/proxies as exact local provider quotes\.
- Managed database: 2 vCPU/8 GiB reference primary and 1 failover copies in\-region; no SLA is guaranteed\. Auth/search/outbox share logical database capacity and are not billed as duplicate databases\.
- OTP volume unknown, assumed range 0 to twice the year\-12 users: upper 600000 messages/month\. SMS rate is an explicit unquoted planning envelope; DLT, taxes and country routing may add fees\.
- Payment assumptions: 0–6000 transactions/month, average USD 50; missing count assumes up to 2% of year\-12 users and missing ticket assumes USD 50\. Percentage/fixed rates are declared envelopes, not verified merchant pricing\. Payout, FX, tax, refunds and chargebacks require separate quotes\.
- Headline estimate and budget fit cover infrastructure/operations only\. Payment and SMS activity fees are separately itemized scenarios and excluded from this total; missing volumes are assumptions, not measured expenditure\.
- 1 vCPU and 2 GiB US East Linux x86 example, 1–2x regional planning allowance; load balancer/network charged separately\.
- Assumed USD/SMS planning envelope only; verify country, tax, DLT and provider quote\. No currency conversion or MSG91 tariff is claimed\.
- Authored backup\-storage envelope with retained copy quantity; no cross\-region copy assumed\.
- Authored hosted build\-minute allowance, assuming included quota at the lower bound\. Paid runners/minutes/artifacts require a repository\-specific quote and spending cap\.
- Authored internet\-egress envelope; actual destination, free quota and routes vary\.
- Authored load\-balancer/NAT/request allowance; subnet/routing/SKU quote required\.
- Authored logs/metrics/request\-operations allowance; redact data and set regional retention/quotas\.
- Authored regional persistent\-storage envelope, including replica copies explicitly in quantity\.
- Authored standard\-storage envelope; requests/lifecycle operations have a separate allowance\.
- Cloud SQL memory reference; a declared proxy for other managed providers, not their quoted rate\.
- Cloud SQL reference CPU with up to 2x geography/SKU allowance; other providers use this declared proxy pending exact quotes\.
- Illustrative 2–3% platform\-fee scenario from the domestic pricing starting point; not a merchant quote\. GST, premium methods, payouts and FX are excluded; no INR/USD conversion is inferred\.
- No separate fixed per\-transaction fee modeled for standard domestic checkout; other merchant/product/settlement fees require a quote and are excluded, not assumed universally free\.

## Blockers, validation and owner actions

- critical: MSG91 OTP is proposed provisionally: end\-to\-end india data residency is NOT established\. Verify tenant/merchant eligibility, processing, logs, backups, delivery partners and contracts before production\. This warning is an explicit exception to verified residency, not approval\.
- critical: Razorpay Checkout is proposed provisionally: end\-to\-end india data residency is NOT established\. Verify tenant/merchant eligibility, processing, logs, backups, delivery partners and contracts before production\. This warning is an explicit exception to verified residency, not approval\.
- critical: Checkout is only the collection integration\. Lending authorization, KYC, double\-entry ledger controls, disbursal/payout product eligibility and EMI mandates require a separately scoped implementation and contractual review; no approval or complete lending product is implied\.
- warning: 99\.95% is a target, not a product guarantee\. The cost model provisions redundancy assumptions; service terms, failover and workload behavior still require verification\.
- warning: The output proposes technical control designs only\. It does not certify compliance, establish legal applicability, execute contracts, or replace an audit\. Implement controls and obtain scope\-specific review\.
- warning: No measured evidence establishes the 300 ms p95 target; load\-test the complete client/network/data path\.
- warning: Planning bands combine published reference rates and explicitly authored allowances; they are not regional provider quotes or measured workload capacity\. Validate sizing, merchant/SMS eligibility, storage, requests and current tariffs before purchase\.
- infrastructure\.data\_residency, requirements\.auth: Request the scoped vendor data\-flow and configuration evidence\. Review a regional alternative without changing the original residency requirement\.
- infrastructure\.data\_residency, requirements\.payments: Request the scoped vendor data\-flow and configuration evidence\. Review a regional alternative without changing the original residency requirement\.
- project\.type, requirements\.payments, compliance: Obtain the missing control/contract evidence and verify implementation; a vendor badge does not approve the application\.

Virginia and Ireland, combined with RDS PostgreSQL product evidence for primary deployment mappings\. Exact engine version/SKU eligibility, backup placement and contracts remain deployment review tasks\.

- core:spring: [Spring Boot SQL](https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/reference/data/sql.html); checked 2026\-11\-13; Java/Kotlin JDBC SQL integration; matching driver required
- services:aws\-logs: [CloudWatch Logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/WhatIsCloudWatchLogs.html); checked 2026\-11\-13; Regional logging configuration required\.
- services:ci: [GitHub Actions](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/about-github-actions/understanding-github-actions); checked 2026\-11\-13; Build only source/synthetic tests; no production data exports\.
- services:fargate\-price: [Fargate pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/fargate/pricing/); checked 2026\-11\-13; US East example Linux x86 CPU/memory rates; regional correction is an explicit assumption\.
- services:gcp\-logs: [Regional Cloud Logging](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/regionalized-logs); checked 2026\-11\-13; Regional log buckets and routing configuration\.
- services:keycloak\-admin: [Keycloak administration](https://www.keycloak.org/docs/latest/server_admin/index.html); checked 2026\-11\-13; Self\-hosted identity, federation and broker configuration; not built\-in SMS OTP\.
- services:keycloak\-db: [Keycloak database support](https://www.keycloak.org/server/db); checked 2026\-11\-13; Relational database support; pin compatible versions\.
- services:msg91: [MSG91 OTP](https://docs.msg91.com/en/otp/sendotp); checked 2026\-11\-13; Phone OTP API; country rules and contracts still required\.
- services:msg91\-privacy: [MSG91 privacy](https://msg91.com/privacy-policy); checked 2026\-11\-13; Multiple hosting geographies; strict residency not established by this source\.
- services:onnx: [ONNX Runtime](https://onnxruntime.ai/docs/get-started/with-java.html); checked 2026\-11\-13; CPU inference requires compatible ONNX model; not GPU training/RAG\.
- services:pg\-tx: [PostgreSQL transactions](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/tutorial-transactions.html); checked 2026\-11\-13; Atomic application/outbox writes; outbox/worker protocol remains custom\.
- services:razorpay\-checkout: [Razorpay Standard Checkout integration](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/payment-gateway/web-integration/standard/); checked 2026\-11\-14; Checkout, server order/payment verification and webhook integration; merchant onboarding and country/product eligibility must be verified\.
- services:razorpay\-pricing: [Razorpay pricing](https://razorpay.com/pricing/); checked 2026\-11\-14; Published domestic pricing starting point; payment mix, GST, payouts and merchant terms require an exact quote\. No USD conversion assumed\.
- services:razorpay\-privacy: [Razorpay privacy policy](https://razorpay.com/privacy-policy/); checked 2026\-11\-13; Candidate regional payment provider privacy terms; not sufficient to approve every merchant, payment product or international data flow\. Not selected by this release\.
- services:s3: [Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/Welcome.html); checked 2026\-11\-13; Regional object storage and configuration responsibilities\.
- services:s3\-price: [S3 pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/s3/pricing/); checked 2026\-11\-13; Storage, requests and egress vary; cross\-provider estimate below is a planning envelope\.
- services:sql\-price: [Cloud SQL pricing](https://cloud.google.com/sql/pricing); checked 2026\-11\-13; Reference CPU $0\.0413/vCPU\-hour and memory $0\.007/GiB\-hour; HA replicas billed; not an India\-specific quote\.
- services:storage\-price: [Cloud Storage pricing](https://cloud.google.com/storage/pricing); checked 2026\-11\-13; Storage, operations and network are distinct charges\.
- services:telemetry: [OpenTelemetry Collector](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/collector/); checked 2026\-11\-13; Collection/redaction/export; backend retention must be configured\.

## Limits and acceptance

- Exploratory analysis only. The original recommendation and original requirements are unchanged.
- Priority stability counts a finite one-at-a-time sweep; it is not a probability, confidence score or exhaustive sensitivity analysis.
- The tradeoff front covers all complete candidates in this finite reviewed catalog, minimizing cost upper bound and operated components while maximizing the ORIGINAL-priority heuristic score. It does not establish real-world optimality or measured architecture quality.
- Functional experiments try eligible single/pair edits only: phone login to email/password, payments off, offline support off, full-text search off, or unsupported ML off. They are changed projects, never solutions satisfying the original brief.
- Within Decision Lab functional experiments, compliance, infrastructure/residency/provider, tenant isolation, availability, budget, team and timeline are never relaxed. A usable hypothetical result is not legal, security or production approval.
- No user assertion authenticates vendor/tenant evidence. Missing contracts, capacity calibration and independent review remain unresolved.
- engine_evaluations counts top-level scenario trials; the baseline recommendation may additionally evaluate one separately labeled budget proposal. Budget proposals are outside the functional-experiment sweep and never change the baseline brief.
- The generated ADR is Proposed; no stakeholder acceptance, implementation or deployment is inferred.

Acceptance, independent review, vendor eligibility, implementation and deployment remain owner tasks. No acceptance is recorded.

No latency SLA or measured framework throughput is credited; embedded-write concurrency is a review heuristic. Low-memory clients require measurement, not an assumed framework benchmark.

Razorpay Checkout is proposed provisionally: end-to-end india data residency is NOT established. Verify tenant/merchant eligibility, processing, logs, backups, delivery partners and contracts before production. This warning is an explicit exception to verified residency, not approval.

limitations: Exploratory analysis only. The original recommendation and original requirements are unchanged.
Priority stability counts a finite one-at-a-time sweep; it is not a probability, confidence score or exhaustive sensitivity analysis.

The tradeoff front covers all complete candidates in this finite reviewed catalog, minimizing cost upper bound and operated components while maximizing the ORIGINAL-priority heuristic score. It does not establish real-world optimality or measured architecture quality.

Functional experiments try eligible single/pair edits only: phone login to email/password, payments off, offline support off, full-text search off, or unsupported ML off. They are changed projects, never solutions satisfying the original brief.

Within Decision Lab functional experiments, compliance, infrastructure/residency/provider, tenant isolation, availability, budget, team and timeline are never relaxed. A usable hypothetical result is not legal, security or production approval.
No user assertion authenticates vendor/tenant evidence. Missing contracts, capacity calibration and independent review remain unresolved.

engine_evaluations counts top-level scenario trials; the baseline recommendation may additionally evaluate one separately labeled budget proposal. Budget proposals are outside the functional-experiment sweep and never change the baseline brief.
